01 / Clinical contextPartial reproduction / medical draft

A non-invasive sample. A translational challenge.

Gastric cancer (GC): can salivary transcriptomics support earlier detection?

From gastric mucosa to a saliva-based liquid biopsy.Accessible sampling is attractive; diagnostic validity must still be established.

Why this paper matters

Lopes et al. compare GC-associated tissue and saliva expression, then evaluate whether saliva requires its own diagnostic signature.

What reproduction asks

Do independent preprocessing and statistical analysis recover the signals, and do prediction claims survive validation safeguards?

Lopes et al., Scientific Reports 15, 18491 (2025). Raw processing, DE and GO completed; modeling and robustness ongoing.STAGE

Set the clinical stage before introducing computational methods. Endoscopy and histopathology remain central to GC diagnosis; this paper does not establish their replacement. Saliva is an accessible liquid-biopsy specimen, but tissue expression and salivary expression need not represent the same biological processes.

The translational question is whether a GC-associated salivary transcriptomic signature can discriminate cases from controls. Do not equate retrospective case-control discrimination with early-stage screening utility. Original GEO data access recovered during the isolated cloud retry. Raw preprocessing of all four cohorts, differential expression and GO/GSEA are now completed. Model fitting and cohort-scale robustness are still pending. Both the original saved saliva outputs and new cloud-computed evidence are identified in the presentation provenance.

02 / Study architecturePublished design / metadata verified

Four cohorts. Two biological compartments.

Internal modeling, external tissue validation and cross-compartment transfer.

DatasetCompartmentGC / controlPublished role
GSE66229400 samplesGastric tissue300 / 100Scenario A: internal tissue

Scenario C applies tissue models to saliva. These are not paired tissue-saliva specimens from the same individuals.

Counts are samples, not necessarily unique patients. No independent external saliva cohort was established.COHORTS

The publication develops models using tissue or saliva, with a stratified 70/30 split and repeated cross-validation in training. Scenario B evaluates source-trained tissue models directly in external tissue cohorts; scenario C transfers tissue models to saliva, and scenario D develops saliva-specific models. The Chinese and Italian cohorts externally validate tissue models, not the saliva classifier.

Some tissue controls are adjacent or patient-matched non-cancer tissue. Cohort counts must not be interpreted as independent unique-patient counts, and the separate saliva and tissue studies are not paired-compartment sampling. GSE66229 is a SuperSeries; duplicate tumor/normal subseries ingestion must be avoided. Metadata counts have been verified, but a metadata audit is not raw-data normalization or numerical replication.

Reproduce the protocol. Do not force the numbers.

Python RMA and moderated DE have not been shown numerically equivalent to affy / limma.

RMA = robust multi-array average; BH = Benjamini-Hochberg; DE = differential expression.METHODS

Use the publication's terminology, while being precise about the independent implementation. PM-only raw RMA includes background correction, quantile normalization and summarization. Two-group empirical-Bayes moderated OLS borrows information across genes to stabilize residual variance, conceptually analogous to limma but not proven numerically identical.

All four completed normalization cohorts use raw-CEL-derived log2 expression without processed-matrix fallback. Four RuntimeWarnings indicate median polish reached its 50-iteration limit at tolerance 1e-6; logs do not identify probe sets or cohorts, and four warnings do not mean exactly four affected probe sets. Numerical affy parity remains unestablished. Filtering uses the global matrix median with declared alternatives. Mapping and implementation differences are plausible explanations, not proven causes of discrepancies. Saliva model candidates are discovered DEGs, not a silently imposed published panel.

04 / Preprocessing concordanceMeasured saliva outputs

The gene universe is an analytical choice.

Mapped genes: 21,367 published versus 20,953 computed. Default retention: 20,407 versus 20,527.

The alternative bars show retained-count sensitivity, not alternative DEG sets or predictive performance.ACTUAL DATA

This is a new visualization of the saved, completed saliva filter sensitivity analysis. All three bars use a common zero-to-22,000 scale; the dashed line is the publication's retained count. The default keeps genes with any sample above the global matrix median. Gene mean above the median retains 11,171; at least half the samples above the median retains 10,014. These alternatives were declared and their counts measured.

The default yields 20,527 genes, 120 more than the publication. It was not adjusted to hit a target. The starting annotation universe is also different: 20,953 versus 21,367. These counts demonstrate sensitivity of feature eligibility; they do not establish how alternative filtering changes DEGs, enrichment or AUC. Input hashes and generator provenance accompany the derived figures.

05 / Differential expressionOriginal computed volcano plots

The direction agrees. The DEG count does not.

Both contrasts: GC minus control; strict |log2FC| > 1 and BH-adjusted P < 0.05. Axes differ.

Original scientific colors and axes preserved.
Same public saliva cohort; independent analytical reproduction, not new-patient validation.ACTUAL DATA

These are original full tested-gene volcano plots, generated by completed raw-derived DE analyses. Tissue retains 15,420 genes versus 14,782 published and yields 1,616 DEGs (662 up, 954 down) versus 1,302 (579 up, 723 down). Saliva retains 20,527 and yields 37 downregulated DEGs, including all 14 published genes. Both cohorts map 20,953 genes.

Group 1 is GC and group 0 is control. Negative log2FC indicates lower expression in GC. Y is -log10 BH-adjusted P, not raw P. Tissue and saliva plots retain different axes, so do not equate visual heights across panels. The modal preserves publication Figure 3D for the original saliva comparison; its statistical quantities and implementations are not assumed numerically matched. This is partial concordance, not exact numerical replication or independent new-patient validation.

06 / Expression structureOriginal reproduction heatmap

An expression pattern is not a diagnostic classifier.

The 37 computed DEGs across all 94 saliva samples, ranked by absolute moderated t statistic.

Full-cohort-selected genes; not held-out discrimination.

This is the original heatmap produced by the reproduction, not a schematic. All 37 DEGs fit under the plotting limit of 50. Rows are ranked by descending absolute moderated t statistic. Each row is standardized to a z-score, and the color scale is displayed from -3 to +3; colors therefore compare relative expression within each gene, not absolute abundance across genes.

The plot preserves input column order and displays accessions. It has no dendrogram or unsupervised clustering, so do not describe it as a discovered patient partition. Clinical labels are in the manifest, not inferred from accession numbers. The DEGs were selected on the complete case-control cohort. A heatmap of those same samples is a descriptive view and cannot demonstrate out-of-sample diagnostic performance. Original scientific colors are intentionally preserved.

07 / Signature concordanceMeasured gene-level effects

Complete recovery. Incomplete numerical agreement.

14 / 14 saliva genes recovered; 23 additional. Computed tissue-saliva overlap: GJB2 and MMP12; paper: zero.

DEG-only display, sorted by log2FC. No error bars or biological independence are claimed.ACTUAL DATA

This new effect-size figure reads each exact log2FC from the saved DEG table. Filled rose circles identify the 14 publication genes: ANKRD37, BAG3, DSP, FRMD4B, JMJD1C, NAA20, RND3, SDR16C5, SEPTIN10, TMPRSS11B, TUFT1, ZBED2, ZFAND2A and ZHX1. Hollow squares identify the 23 additional significant genes. All effect sizes are computed, not published estimates; no confidence intervals are invented.

The completed tissue-saliva overlap is two genes, GJB2 and MMP12, both among the additional saliva DEGs. The publication reported zero overlap. This is an analytical discrepancy, not proof of a shared causal mechanism or tissue origin for salivary RNA. A larger set is not automatically better biological discovery. Full overlap records are transferred and SHA256-verified locally.

08 / Diagnostic discriminationCompleted models / robustness pending

Recovered genes. Unreproduced discrimination.

Scenario D: 37 discovered saliva DEGs; 29-sample holdout. Publication: 14-gene panel.

SVM sensitivity: 0 / 19 GC at threshold 0.5

Full-cohort DE risks selection leakage. Bootstrap CIs condition on fitted models, not the entire pipeline.

Different discovered panels and implementations; no AUC inversion or outcome relabeling. No external saliva validation.ACTUAL COMPARISON

Paired points and 95% CIs compare publication Table 3 with actual saliva held-out estimates. Computed AUCs are RF 0.721, GBM 0.684, DT 0.668 and SVM 0.311. Published SVM AUC is 0.868 (0.721-0.974); computed SVM is 0.311 (0.084-0.558). All axes span zero to one. The poor SVM result is not inverted, relabeled, or substituted with another model. The modal includes genuine original ROC curves and all scenario AUCs, independently checked against stored predictions.

The saliva holdout contains 19 GC and 10 control samples. At threshold 0.5, SVM predicts all as control: sensitivity 0, specificity 1, accuracy 10/29. PPV and LR+ are undefined, not zero. Reproduction uses all 37 discovered DEGs rather than the fixed published 14. Tissue selected CEMIP, ADIPOQ, LIFR, PACC1, ESM1, GPX3 and TMT1A; only ESM1 and TMT1A match the published seven. Internal tissue AUCs are 0.967-0.997, external Chinese tissue 0.703-0.839, external Italian tissue 0.684-0.986; tissue-to-saliva 0.458-0.500.

These are the faithful full-cohort-DE branch, with selection leakage, not robustness-corrected estimates. CIs use 2,000 stratified bootstraps conditional on the fitted model and omit feature-selection/tuning variability. Cohort-wide RMA remains transductive. Robustness remains incomplete; its live process state is unverified after remote continuation-message admission failed. No independent clinical saliva validation is established.

09 / Biological interpretationCompleted GO preranked enrichment

Pathway signals recur. Enrichment claims diverge.

Tissue includes DNA replication signals; saliva has 88 significant BP terms, unlike the publication's reported absence.

Significant termsTissueSaliva
Biological process40288
Cellular component7153
Molecular function5939

All significant saliva terms have negative NES. Different FDR methods limit numerical comparability.

Leading computed BP terms

Tissue: DNA metabolic process NES +2.884; DNA replication +2.845.

Saliva: COPII-coated vesicle budding NES -2.318; translational initiation regulation -2.269.

GO 2023; signed moderated-t ranking; 1,000 permutations.

Per-ontology GSEA FDR < 0.05 is not clusterProfiler adjusted P. Zero empirical FDR is not mathematical zero.ACTUAL DATA

The completed gseapy 1.3.2 prerank analysis ranks all retained genes by signed moderated t descending, breaking ties by gene name. Parameters: GO 2023 snapshots, seed 2025, 1,000 permutations, min_size 15, max_size 500, one thread. Significant terms at per-ontology FDR below 0.05 are tissue BP/CC/MF 402/71/59, saliva 88/53/39. All significant saliva terms have negative NES. Positive NES is GC-associated and negative NES is control-associated under this contrast.

Broad tissue replication/cell-cycle biology is consistent with parts of the paper, but saliva's absence of significant BP enrichment is not reproduced. These are not numerically identical methods: gseapy permutation FDR is not clusterProfiler adjusted P. GO version, gene universe, ranking and preprocessing also affect comparisons. Finite-permutation q-values printed as zero are empirical estimates, not mathematical zeros. The original source-verified figures in the modal show the top four significant terms per ontology by absolute NES, not every significant term.

A recovered signature. Not a validated liquid biopsy.

Analytical concordance, numerical replication and clinical utility are different endpoints.

All four cohorts raw-processed.

Tissue replication-related GO signals.

Measured deviations

Tissue DEGs: 1,616 vs 1,302.
Saliva: 37 vs 14.
Overlap: 2 vs 0.

Clinical requirements

Independent prospective saliva validation, intended-use population, early-stage performance and decision utility.

Models completed: saliva SVM AUC 0.311, not published 0.868. Full robustness results remain unavailable.

Independent implementation, not numerical affy/limma parity. No external saliva validation or screening utility established.CONCLUSION

Distinguish analytical agreement from exact replication and clinical utility. Raw RMA completed across 695 samples in four cohorts without fallback. Tissue and saliva DE, GO and model results are now measured, with important deviations in counts, overlap, saliva BP enrichment and saliva classification. Original source records and PNG hashes are preserved locally. Four median-polish nonconvergence warnings remain an interpretation caveat, not an automatic assertion of invalid results or exactly four affected probe sets.

The full default cloud run has no verified terminal robustness result. One tissue RF same-holdout fold-local-DE subcheck completed: AUC 0.9948 versus faithful-branch 0.9970, with 120 verified identical holdout IDs. The model inspection panel visualizes these point estimates without inventing a fold-local CI. This single result is not a full robustness assessment; split/permutation/stability conclusions remain unavailable. Later continuation-message admission failed, so live process status is unknown, not proof of completion or failure. Supervised full-cohort DE before splitting risks selection leakage; training-local feature selection is needed inside CV, but cohort-wide RMA still uses test-cohort information for transductive preprocessing. Clinical translation further requires independent prospective saliva validation in the intended-use population, calibration, predictive values at screening prevalence, early-stage performance and decision utility. No screening test is validated by recovering a gene list.

Interpretation limits

Same public cohorts, not new patients. No established affy/limma numerical parity. Four median-polish nonconvergence warnings do not identify specific affected cohorts or probe sets. gseapy per-ontology permutation FDR is not clusterProfiler adjusted P; zero empirical FDR is not mathematical zero. Full-cohort DE risks selection leakage; cohort-wide RMA remains transductive. Independent clinical saliva validation is not established.

Computed AUC CIs use 2,000 stratified bootstrap replicates, conditional on fitted models, not the whole pipeline. SVM saliva outcomes or AUC direction are not reversed. Undefined PPV and LR+ remain undefined; infinite LR+ in source records remains infinite.

One completed tissue RF same-holdout fold-local-DE subcheck gives AUC 0.9948 versus 0.9970 in the full-cohort-DE branch. tissue-rf-fold-local.json records the verified 120-sample holdout, selected genes and source/prediction hashes. This does not complete split resampling, permutation, stability or shift checks. Full-cohort RMA remains transductive.
